name: base
title: Maths and general science
summary: SAT, SMT and optimisation solvers, computer algebra, graph generation, exact and numerical Python, compilers, readers for the usual data and document formats, and light libraries for chemistry, biology and astronomy.

tools.name: kissat
tools.does: SAT solver, usually the fastest here; can write a proof of unsatisfiability
tools.usage: kissat FILE.cnf   |   kissat FILE.cnf PROOF.drat
tools.check:
printf 'p cnf 1 2
1 0
-1 0
' > t.cnf; kissat -q t.cnf; true

tools.name: cadical
tools.does: SAT solver
tools.usage: cadical FILE.cnf
tools.check:
printf 'p cnf 1 2
1 0
-1 0
' > t.cnf; cadical -q t.cnf; true

tools.name: minisat
tools.does: SAT solver, small and classic
tools.usage: minisat FILE.cnf OUT
tools.check:
printf 'p cnf 1 2
1 0
-1 0
' > t.cnf; minisat t.cnf out >/dev/null 2>&1; cat out

tools.name: drat-trim
tools.does: checks a SAT solver's proof of unsatisfiability, independently of the solver
tools.usage: kissat FILE.cnf PROOF.drat; drat-trim FILE.cnf PROOF.drat
tools.check:
printf 'p cnf 2 4
1 2 0
-1 2 0
1 -2 0
-1 -2 0
' > t.cnf; kissat -q t.cnf t.drat >/dev/null; drat-trim t.cnf t.drat

tools.name: pysat
tools.does: SAT solvers from Python (CaDiCaL, Glucose and others), with encodings for cardinality constraints
tools.usage: python: from pysat.solvers import Cadical153; from pysat.formula import CNF; from pysat.card import CardEnc
tools.check: python -c "from pysat.solvers import Cadical153; s=Cadical153(bootstrap_with=[[1],[-1]]); print('answer', 'sat' if s.solve() else 'unsat')"

tools.name: z3
tools.does: SMT solver: integers, reals, bit-vectors, arrays, quantifiers
tools.usage: z3 FILE.smt2   |   python: import z3
tools.check: python -c "import z3; x=z3.Int('x'); s=z3.Solver(); s.add(x*x==49, x>0); print(s.check(), s.model()[x])"

tools.name: ortools
tools.does: CP-SAT: constraint and integer programming, good at scheduling and combinatorial search
tools.usage: python: from ortools.sat.python import cp_model
tools.check: python -c "from ortools.sat.python import cp_model as c; m=c.CpModel(); x=m.NewIntVar(0,10,'x'); m.Add(2*x==14); s=c.CpSolver(); s.Solve(m); print('x =', s.Value(x))"

tools.name: highs
tools.does: linear and mixed-integer programming (HiGHS). Use it in a script of its own: it cannot be loaded together with ortools
tools.usage: python: import highspy
tools.check: python -c "import highspy; print('highs', type(highspy.Highs()).__name__)"

tools.name: scip
tools.does: global mixed-integer nonlinear optimisation, with a proof of optimality
tools.usage: python: from pyscipopt import Model
tools.check: python -c "from pyscipopt import Model; m=Model(); m.hideOutput(); x=m.addVar(lb=0,ub=4); m.setObjective(x,'maximize'); m.optimize(); print('best', m.getObjVal())"

tools.name: pari-gp
tools.does: number theory: factoring, primality, number fields, elliptic curves, modular forms
tools.usage: gp -q FILE.gp
tools.check: echo 'print(factor(2^64+1))' | gp -q

tools.name: gap
tools.does: group theory and discrete algebra (core packages)
tools.usage: gap -q FILE.g
tools.check: printf '%s\n' 'Print(Size(SymmetricGroup(5)));' | gap -q

tools.name: singular
tools.does: commutative algebra and algebraic geometry: Gröbner bases, ideals, resolutions
tools.usage: Singular -q FILE.sing
tools.check: echo 'ring r=0,(x,y),dp; ideal i=x2+y2-1,x-y; print(std(i)); quit;' | Singular -q

tools.name: nauty
tools.does: generates graphs up to isomorphism and computes canonical forms and automorphism groups
tools.usage: geng -c N   |   genbg, labelg, shortg, countg   |   python: import pynauty
tools.check: geng -c 5 2>/dev/null | wc -l

tools.name: networkx
tools.does: graph algorithms in Python
tools.usage: python: import networkx as nx
tools.check: python -c "import networkx as nx; print('petersen', nx.petersen_graph().number_of_edges())"

tools.name: sympy
tools.does: symbolic mathematics: algebra, calculus, exact arithmetic
tools.usage: python: import sympy
tools.check: python -c "import sympy; print(sympy.factorint(2**32+1))"

tools.name: flint and mpmath
tools.does: fast exact arithmetic on integers and polynomials (flint); arbitrary-precision real and complex numbers (mpmath)
tools.usage: python: import flint, mpmath
tools.check: python -c "import flint, mpmath; mpmath.mp.dps=30; print(flint.fmpz(2)**100, mpmath.zeta(2))"

tools.name: numpy stack
tools.does: numerical computing, data frames, statistics, machine learning and plots (plots are saved to files; there is no display)
tools.usage: python: numpy, scipy, pandas, statsmodels, sklearn, matplotlib
tools.check: python -c "import numpy, scipy, pandas, statsmodels, sklearn, matplotlib; print('stack ok', numpy.linalg.det(numpy.eye(3)))"

tools.name: rdkit
tools.does: cheminformatics: molecules from SMILES, descriptors, substructure search, conformers
tools.usage: python: from rdkit import Chem
tools.check: python -c "from rdkit import Chem; print('atoms', Chem.MolFromSmiles('CCO').GetNumAtoms())"

tools.name: biopython
tools.does: sequences, alignments and common bioinformatics file formats
tools.usage: python: from Bio import SeqIO
tools.check: python -c "from Bio.Seq import Seq; print(Seq('ATGC').reverse_complement())"

tools.name: astropy
tools.does: astronomy: units, coordinates, time, FITS files, cosmology
tools.usage: python: import astropy
tools.check: python -c "import astropy.units as u; print((1*u.pc).to(u.lyr))"

tools.name: data file readers
tools.does: reads SPSS, Stata and SAS files (pyreadstat) and R .rds and .RData files (pyreadr)
tools.usage: python: import pyreadstat, pyreadr
tools.check: python -c "import pyreadstat, pyreadr; print('readers ok')"

tools.name: pdf tools
tools.does: turns PDFs into text, and pulls tables out of them
tools.usage: pdftotext -layout FILE.pdf OUT.txt   |   pdfinfo FILE.pdf   |   python: import pypdf   |   import pdfplumber; pdfplumber.open(FILE).pages[0].extract_table()
tools.check: pdftotext -v 2>&1 | head -1; python -c "import pypdf, pdfplumber; print('pypdf ok')"

tools.name: archives
tools.does: packs and unpacks zip, 7z, zstd, gzip, bzip2, xz and tar files
tools.usage: unzip FILE.zip -d DIR   |   zip -r OUT.zip DIR   |   7z x FILE.7z   |   zstd -d FILE.zst   |   tar xf FILE.tar.gz
tools.check: printf 'zipped ok\n' > a.txt && zip -q a.zip a.txt && unzip -p a.zip && zstd -qf a.txt && 7z t a.zip > /dev/null && echo done

tools.name: file inspection
tools.does: says what kind of file something is, searches text fast, shows bytes and folder trees
tools.usage: file FILE   |   rg PATTERN [DIR]   |   xxd FILE | head   |   tree DIR   |   less FILE
tools.check: printf 'needle\n' > f.txt; rg -c needle f.txt; file -b f.txt; xxd f.txt | head -1 > /dev/null; tree --version > /dev/null && echo done

tools.name: jq
tools.does: reads, filters and reshapes JSON on the command line
tools.usage: jq '.field' FILE.json   |   jq -r '.items[] | [.a, .b] | @tsv' FILE.json

tools.name: sqlite
tools.does: SQL database in one file; also good for querying CSV files
tools.usage: sqlite3 FILE.db 'select ...'   |   sqlite3 :memory: -cmd '.mode csv' -cmd '.import data.csv t' 'select count(*) from t'   |   python: import sqlite3
tools.check: sqlite3 :memory: 'select 6*7'

tools.name: shell tools
tools.does: gawk for text columns, bc for exact arithmetic, GNU parallel to run many small commands side by side
tools.usage: gawk '{s+=$2} END {print s}' FILE   |   echo '2^200' | bc   |   parallel -j $PHS_CPUS ./job.sh {} ::: 1 2 3
tools.check: echo '2^64' | bc; echo 'a 5' | gawk '{print $2*2}'; parallel -k echo job{} ::: 1 2 2>/dev/null

tools.name: spreadsheets
tools.does: reads and writes Excel (.xlsx, .xls) and LibreOffice (.ods) files; pandas.read_excel works
tools.usage: python: pandas.read_excel('FILE.xlsx', sheet_name=None)   |   import openpyxl, xlrd, odf
tools.check: python -c "import openpyxl, xlrd, odf, pandas as pd; wb = openpyxl.Workbook(); wb.active['A1'] = 42; wb.save('/tmp/t.xlsx'); print('sheet', pd.read_excel('/tmp/t.xlsx', header=None).iloc[0, 0])"

tools.name: documents and markup
tools.does: reads HTML and XML (lxml, BeautifulSoup, xmltodict), Word files (python-docx), and guesses text encodings (chardet)
tools.usage: python: from bs4 import BeautifulSoup   |   import lxml.etree   |   import xmltodict, docx, chardet
tools.check:
python -c "from bs4 import BeautifulSoup; import lxml.etree as E, xmltodict, chardet, docx; print(BeautifulSoup('

soup ok

', 'lxml').p.text, E.fromstring('7').findtext('b'))"

tools.name: hdf5
tools.does: reads and writes HDF5 files (h5py), a common format for large scientific arrays
tools.usage: python: import h5py; f = h5py.File('FILE.h5'); list(f)
tools.check: python -c "import h5py, numpy as np; f = h5py.File('/tmp/t.h5', 'w'); f['x'] = np.arange(10); f.close(); print('h5 sum', int(h5py.File('/tmp/t.h5')['x'][:].sum()))"

tools.name: parquet and arrow
tools.does: reads and writes Parquet and Feather files (pyarrow); pandas.read_parquet works
tools.usage: python: pandas.read_parquet('FILE.parquet')   |   import pyarrow.parquet as pq
tools.check: python -c "import pandas as pd; pd.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2, 3]}).to_parquet('/tmp/t.parquet'); print('parquet sum', int(pd.read_parquet('/tmp/t.parquet')['a'].sum()))"

tools.name: netcdf and xarray
tools.does: labelled multi-dimensional arrays (xarray) and NetCDF files (netCDF4)
tools.usage: python: import xarray as xr; ds = xr.open_dataset('FILE.nc')
tools.check: python -c "import xarray as xr, numpy as np; xr.Dataset({'t': ('x', np.arange(4.0))}).to_netcdf('/tmp/t.nc'); print('nc mean', float(xr.open_dataset('/tmp/t.nc')['t'].mean()))"

tools.name: duckdb
tools.does: fast SQL straight on CSV and Parquet files, including ones too large for pandas
tools.usage: python: import duckdb; duckdb.sql("select count(*) from 'FILE.csv'").show()
tools.check: python -c "import duckdb; print('duck', duckdb.sql('select 6*7').fetchone()[0])"

tools.name: polars
tools.does: fast data frames, with lazy reading of files larger than memory
tools.usage: python: import polars as pl; pl.scan_csv('FILE.csv').group_by('k').agg(pl.col('v').mean()).collect()
tools.check: python -c "import polars as pl; print('polars', pl.DataFrame({'a': [1, 2, 3]}).select(pl.col('a').sum()).item())"

tools.name: numba and cython
tools.does: makes numerical Python loops run at compiled speed
tools.usage: python: from numba import njit   |   cythonize -i FILE.pyx
tools.check: python -c "import numba, Cython; f = numba.njit(lambda n: n * (n + 1) // 2); print('jit', f(100))"

tools.name: gmpy2
tools.does: fast exact arithmetic on very large integers and rationals, and primality tests (GMP, MPFR)
tools.usage: python: import gmpy2; gmpy2.is_prime(n); gmpy2.mpz(2)**1000
tools.check: python -c "import gmpy2; print(gmpy2.is_prime(2**127 - 1), gmpy2.fac(25))"

tools.name: cvxpy and pulp
tools.does: modelling languages for convex optimisation (cvxpy) and linear or integer programs (pulp, with HiGHS as solver)
tools.usage: python: import cvxpy as cp   |   import pulp; prob.solve(pulp.HiGHS(msg=False))
tools.check: python -c "import cvxpy as cp, pulp; x = cp.Variable(); cp.Problem(cp.Minimize((x - 3) ** 2)).solve(); print('cvx', round(float(x.value), 3))"

tools.name: igraph
tools.does: fast graph algorithms on large graphs: communities, paths, isomorphism, structural measures
tools.usage: python: import igraph as ig
tools.check: python -c "import igraph as ig; print('girth', ig.Graph.Famous('Petersen').girth())"

tools.name: seaborn and pingouin
tools.does: statistical plots (seaborn) and the common statistical tests with effect sizes (pingouin)
tools.usage: python: import seaborn as sns   |   import pingouin as pg; pg.ttest(x, y)
tools.check: python -c "import seaborn, pingouin as pg; print('effect', pg.compute_effsize([1, 2, 3], [1, 2, 3]))"

tools.name: compilers
tools.does: C, C++ and Fortran compilers with make and cmake, for writing a fast search program or building small numerical codes
tools.usage: gcc -O2 -o prog prog.c   |   g++ -O2 -std=c++17 -o prog prog.cpp   |   gfortran -O2 -o prog prog.f90   |   cmake -B build && cmake --build build
tools.check:
printf 'program t
 print *, 6*7
end program
' > t.f90 && gfortran t.f90 -o t_f && ./t_f && printf '#include <stdio.h>
int main(){printf("c ok\n");}
' > t.c && gcc t.c -o t_c && ./t_c && cmake --version | head -1

tools.name: graphviz
tools.does: draws graphs and diagrams from a text description
tools.usage: dot -Tsvg IN.dot -o OUT.svg   |   neato -Tpng IN.dot -o OUT.png
tools.check: echo 'digraph{a->b}' | dot -Tsvg | grep -c '<svg'

tools.name: tesseract
tools.does: reads the text out of scanned pages and images (OCR, English), for papers that have no text layer
tools.usage: pdftoppm -r 300 -png FILE.pdf page && tesseract page-1.png out   (writes out.txt)
tools.check: python -c "from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont; im = Image.new('L', (520, 120), 255); ImageDraw.Draw(im).text((20, 25), 'HELLO 42', font=ImageFont.load_default(size=56), fill=0); im.save('/tmp/ocr.png')" && tesseract /tmp/ocr.png - 2>/dev/null

tools.name: python helpers
tools.does: testing (pytest, hypothesis), progress bars (tqdm), text tables (tabulate) and JSON schema checks (jsonschema)
tools.usage: pytest -q   |   python: from hypothesis import given   |   from tqdm import tqdm   |   from tabulate import tabulate
tools.check: python -c "import pytest, hypothesis, tqdm, jsonschema; from tabulate import tabulate; print(tabulate([['helpers', 'ok']], tablefmt='plain'))"
